stoichiometric reaction of 11 with 1c in the absence of aryl

Interestingly, when an additional 1.5 equiv of 4-chloroiodo-
benzene (2b) was employed as the coupling reagent, it was
found that the 4-chloroaryl-substituted allene 3cb was obtained
in 54% yield, but still with only 5% of product 12 originated
from the “precatalyst” 11 (Scheme 4e, eq 3). The low yield of
product 12 seems insuficient to support an arylnickel(II)
species as a feasible intermediate in the catalytic cycle, and the
mechanism that directs trapping of the propargyl/allenyl
radical derived from MHAT by an arylnickel(II) species to
form Ni(III) species followed by reductive elimination to form
coupled products can be excluded (the aryl iodide was not
consumed).<sup>15</sup> Meanwhile, in the absence of an oxidative agent,
the continuous production of Co−H is also halted.
Theoretically, at most, 10% of the C−C coupling products
will be formed. These results further encouraged us to consider
that Ni(II) complex 11 might transform into an active Ni
catalyst (e.g., Ni(I)) to prompt the reaction to occur.

intermediate 11 was synthesized (Scheme 4d) and evaluated in
control experiments.<sup>14</sup> When complex 11 was employed as the
nickel precatalyst in the reaction of 1,3-enyne (1c) with ethyl

obtained in 58% yield (Scheme 4e, eq 1). In contrast, a
stoichiometric reaction of 11 with 1c in the absence of aryl

mechanism that directs trapping of the propargyl/allenyl

propargyl radical A, which equilibrates with the allenyl radical
B and is trapped by Co(II) to form a metastable allenyl
cobalt(III) species

more accurately described as an
equilibrium of a cage-pair.<sup>3,17</sup> In the nickel catalytic cycle,

■ CONCLUSION
In summary, we have developed an eficient MHAT-mediated
1,4-hydroarylation of 1,3-enynes with aryl halides via
synergistic cobalt/nickel catalysis. This MHAT-mediated
protocol provides direct access to diverse tetrasubstituted
allenes in high yields. These allene products serve as versatile
synthetic platforms for further elaboration through alkene
functionalization. This work expands the arsenal of MHAT
reactions by merging Co−H-mediated MHAT with Ni-
catalyzed cross-coupling, ofering a novel strategy for allene
synthesis. Studies on the mechanism and development of
enantioselective variants are currently underway.
